messages: Olivia (ProdPM): Hey team — customers reporting p95 regressions on /v1/generate since ~2026-03-16 18:00 UTC. Baseline p95 was ~1.1s, now ~2.7s. Affected model: redwood-4o-open. Seen across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Sample request ids from client logs: rq_2026-03-16_00a1, rq_2026-03-16_01b2. Also ~0.3% 502s. Need a concise repro pack we can hand off to SRE/eng.
messages_followup_2: 1) a single-request curl that reproduces a slow/given response (include `--include` so we can see headers), 2) a concurrency run (wrk/k6/wrk2) that shows p95 spike, 3) HAR or curl traces for ~10 slow requests, 4) token counts and prompt set (short/medium/long), 5) a list of the exact request ids you saw. also please note whether the client is using streaming or non-streaming. :thumbsup:
messages_followup_3:
Michael (Eng): quick example curl to capture headers and request-id:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  --include 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-4o-open","input":"<your prompt here>","max_tokens":256}'
```

Note the response headers: `X-Request-Id` and `X-Redwood-Node`. If you want raw wire traces: `curl --trace-ascii curl.trace ...` and attach the trace. For streaming, use `--no-buffer` and capture stdout. Also paste the full response headers for any 502s.
messages_followup_4:
Raj (SRE): for concurrency runs we prefer k6 or wrk. Example wrk command we asked customers to run (simple):

```bash
wrk -t12 -c48 -d60s -R200 --latency 
  -s scripts/post.lua https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Or a tiny k6 script to POST with a seed prompt file if you prefer. When you run it, capture: concurrency (threads/conns), target RPS, test duration, and percent token distribution (avg tokens per response). Please run three sizes: ~64 tokens, ~320 tokens, ~1024 tokens. That gives us a token matrix to find knee points.
messages_followup_5: Olivia (ProdPM): OK I'll run that now. Our quick notes: we saw the spike at ~18:04 UTC, concurrency on our side was 24 workers, ~180 RPS sustained for 2mins, avg tokens ~320. We'll upload: a) one curl single request with headers, b) two wrk runs (64 / 320 / 1024), c) HAR for ~8 slow requests, d) our seed promptset (5 prompts). Also masking IPs. Any special artifact you want?
messages_followup_6:
Eva (Support): perfect. Two extra asks: 1) include a short CSV with request_id, client_send_ms, server_first_byte_ms, total_ms (helps correlate), 2) if you can run the `support-debug` helper it will bundle logs for us. Example upload endpoint: 

```bash
# from your machine (will generate a token link)
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SUPPORT_TOKEN' 
  -F 'bundle=@debug-bundle.tar.gz' 
  -F 'meta=concurrency:24,rps:180,avg_tokens:320' 
  https://support.redwood.ai/api/v1/debug-bundles
```

If you can't run the helper, just attach the traces and HAR in the ticket. We'll open an internal repro pack and tag eng/sre.
messages_followup_7: Michael (Eng): small tip — include both the client request body and the server response headers for any slow sample. If possible, show whether the same request id was routed to different nodes (`X-Redwood-Node`) — that tells us if this is a routing/kv-cache miss. Also provide your model config (batching enabled/disabled, quant profile if any). If you suspect billing/auth issues, include a curl showing `401` with the token and the account id header (don't paste secrets).
messages_followup_8: Olivia (ProdPM): uploading now. Attached a zip with: single_request.txt (curl + headers), wrk_64.log, wrk_320.log, wrk_1024.log, har_files/, promptset.csv, request_timings.csv. Uploaded to the ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/5643. Note: one of the request ids (rq_2026-03-16_01b2) had a 502 with X-Redwood-Node: node-7 and the rest were node-3. Masked IPs.
